newsitem.title: UK: Sterling at 6-year peak, Euro stocks rebound.
newsitem.headline: Sterling at 6-year peak, Euro stocks rebound.

text.p: The British pound bounded over three marks for the first time in 6-1/2 years on Friday with traders lured by prospects of higher interest rates, dragging the dollar up to a six-year peak in its wake.
European bourses also ended the day with heavy gains, given an extra lift by a strong start on Wall Street. Frankfurt continued its record-breaking pace by closing at a new peak.
Much of the excitement was in currency markets where sterling hit 3.001 marks, its highest since October 1990, capping a year-long rally which has won gains of 30 percent on the German currency.
"Economists are getting trampled in the rush," said Mark Cliffe, chief international economist at HSBC Markets.
"They can say the pound is overvalued for all they are worth but all traders can see is pound signs as rates are going higher."

The surge encountered little resistance from the Bank of England, according to traders, who said there was no sign yet of any central bank intervention to halt its rally, seen as harming parts of the exporting sector.
The pound, which fell back to 2.9978 marks near the European close, also reached $1.6986, its strongest since January 10.
Initial market disappointment that interest rates rose by only a quarter percentage point on Thursday soon gave way to expectations that more increases are on the way.

"The market has come to its senses and realised that a quarter point rate rise yesterday does not preclude more rate rises, probably substantial ones," said Steve Hannah, the director of economic research at IBJ International. "It is difficult to see sterling backing down even from three marks."

Concern that the planned European single currency will not be as strong as the mark and the fact that the pound is not tied to the mark in the European Exchange Rate Mechanism have also helped the pound climb against a broad range of currencies.
The sterling rally against the mark helped to push the dollar up by nearly two pfennigs to 1.7705 marks near the European close, its highest level since August 1991.
"The dollar's climb today is really all down to sterling/mark," said a U.S. bank analyst, as traders ignored German central bank warnings about excessive mark weakness.

"If the Bundesbank does nothing to stop a sustained move in dollar/mark above these levels, we could see the mark falling significantly everywhere, a move that would be totally inconsistent with their public calls for stable exchange rates," said Teis Knuthsen, economist at First Chicago in London.

The mark gleaned only fleeting support from Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer who said on Thursday the dollar's correction from 1995 lows against the mark was over and the Bundesbank wanted a strong mark moving into European economic and monetary union.
In equities, Frankfurt regained its form after dipping nearly two percent on Thursday to make hefty gains. Dealers said the rally was likely to keep on rolling as conditions remained ideal.

"I can't think of any negative factors, we have the best of all possible scenarios for the share market," one Frankfurt share trader said. "My only slight fear is that people are piling into the stock market without really knowing what they are buying."
Floor trade in Frankfurt closed up 1.2 percent at 4,040.97 points on the DAX index but dealings on the after-hours computerised IBIS index soared to a new closing peak of 4,074.30.
The strong dollar was helping Frankfurt's bull run as it improved prospects for the exporting sector. Investors' optimism was also encouraged by low interest rates and inflation-free growth.

London climbed nearly 0.7 percent at the finish, the third successive close in the plus column, lifted by Wall Street. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 0.6 percent near the end of European trade.
Dealers said UK shares looked good for further gains having survived a succession of body blows in recent days -- including Thursday's quarter-point rise in bank lending rates.

"Sometime we will see a violent correction but the market could be 10 percent higher before that happens," said one dealer. "We have been bearish and we have been burnt and I don't want to get caught short again."
In Paris, stocks made only modest advances in light trade ahead of the long Bastille Day holiday weekend.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was at 113.85 yen and 1.7705 marks compared with 113.12 and 1.7534 in late European trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed up 31.7 points at 4799.5
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended up 48.59 points at 4,040.97. The IBIS DAX finished up 73.65 at 4,074.30 points.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed up 12.50 points at 2,941.59.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $320.05 an ounce, compared with Thursday's close of $319.65. Silver was at $4.39, up five cents.
